the E_8-manifolds are the same 4- dimensional manifold, the singular fibers of the E8-elliptic surface are perturbations of a collection of fishtailembolism, and the E8- and E7- elliptic surfaces have rich degenerations of regular to singular fiber.
the E_8-manifolds are indeed the same manifold (and not just diffeomorphic), and that the perturbation of a singular fiber to a fishtail is a handle slide of a regular fiber.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we can now prove all the theorems in the original paper [Gompf 1989] in the case of the E_8-manifolds, and that the proof is much more direct than the original one.

the E_8-manfold is the only closed 4-manifold that can be represented as a union of 4-sphere bundles over S^2, and that it can be obtained by a single perturbation of a regular fiber of an elliptic surface.
the E_8-manfold is an explicit example of Gromov compactness, and that it has an infinite family of distinct handlebody decompositions, each of which is a perturbation of a singular fiber.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
`the E_8-manifolds are the only 4-manifolds which can be obtained from a regular fiber of an elliptic surface by a sequence of surgeries on a single link'.
we give an efficient way to compute the handle picture of an arbitrary singular fiber in a genus 2 elliptic surface.

the E_8-manifolds, which have been studied by many people in the last decade, are the only 4-manifolds with non-trivial Seiberg-Witten invariants that admit handlebody decompositions of a certain kind.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the E_8-manifolds are very special, in that they are the only 4-manifolds with the following three properties: (i) they have a handle decomposition with a single 1-handle; (ii) they have a single nontrivial Seiberg-Witten invariant; and (iii) they have a unique spin structure.
the E_8-manifolds and their perturbations can be understood in terms of a single handlebody decomposition.
the E_8-manifolds can be viewed as `building blocks' for the construction of many 4-manifolds.
